newsitem.title: KENYA: Mission evacuates Zaire station after looting.
newsitem.headline: Mission evacuates Zaire station after looting.

text.p: A missionary group said on Friday it had evacuated its staff and their families from a remote mission station in northeast Zaire after it was looted by Zairean troops.

Herman van Heuvelen, operation manager in Uganda for Mission Aviation Fellowship (MAF), told Reuters by telephone from Kampala that Zairean soldiers fired into the air and stole equipment from the mission on Thursday.
He said all the staff had since left the mission, at Nyakunde 10 miles (18 km) southwest of the town of Bunia near Lake Albert.
"Bunia is very, very tense," he said. "We're not flying in to Bunia at all at the moment."
Andrew Hunt, a worker with Christian Aid, also reported Bunia tense during a visit earlier this week. He said people were afraid of a rebel attack.

No firm information has emerged so far of a rebel presence in the Bunia region, which is about 400 km (250 miles) north of Goma, scene of the fiercest fighting between rebels and the Zairean army since an insurrection began in eastern Zaire last month.
Goma is now in rebel hands, as are other towns further to the south, and the effects of the uprising are being felt over an ever larger area.

Heuvelen said the Zairean soldiers took a truck, a motorcycle and some equipment, but did not harm anyone. He said he believed about nine to 10 families had been evacuated to elsewhere in Zaire and to Kenya.
